To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the direct algebraic restoration of STI in the Abelian model is possible, that the solution depends on the choice of the normalization conditions, that the consistency conditions are satisfied and that the method can be generalized to non-Abelian models.

the restoration of ST identities is possible, even when the counterterms are introduced in an intermediate renormalization scheme, provided that the counterterms are expressed in terms of finite quantities, that the basis of counter-terms is chosen properly and that the consistency conditions are obeyed.

a. the restoration of ST identities can be performed directly in a purely algebraic way, without the evaluation of breaking terms; b. there are many different solutions, corresponding to a different choice of normalization conditions; c. there are consistency conditions to be satisfied, that are necessary for a consistent restoration of ST identities; d. the restoration is not possible if BRST transformations are no longer nilpotent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the restoration of ST identities in the Abelina Higgs-Kibble theory.
the algebraic aspects of renormalization, in the case where the Slavnov-Tayler identities are broken by intermediate renormlization.
the restoration of Slavnova-Taylor identities in gauge theories.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the method of algebraic restoration of the ST identities is feasible, but the problem is still far from being solved.
, in the absence of anomalies, the STI are recovered by the direct algebraic method, provided a set of consistency conditions is obeyed.
, in the Abelian case, the restoration of ST identities is possible, but it is not unique.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, if we are able to impose the STI, we can recover a gauge invariant theory, even in the presence of a non vanishing gauge field mass.
the algebraic method is able to recover STI, provided that the consistency conditions are obeyed.
the STI are restored in a purely algebraic way, by means of a linear problem which is over-determined.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in order to recover STI, it is not necessary to know the explicit form of the counterterms, but it is sufficient to impose the STI directly on the vertex function.
a consistent solution of STI can be achieved only in the case of nilpotent transformations.
, if a consistent choice of normalization conditions and consistency conditions is possible, the restoration of the STI can be carried out without any explicit calculation of the breaking terms.
